label: Good-general favouring is apprehension, from individuation of non-present candidates
description: Let b have a favouring determination whose profile phi is good-general: at some scenario s, for candidates x and y, at least one not a present input, phi depends on betterness with end-realization fixed, so in particular phi favours x over y at s. By item realization phi at s is the inverse image of an item relation under b's stand-in assignment; by irreflexivity phi does not favour y over y. If x and y had the same stand-in, phi would favour y over y, so their stand-ins differ (unindividuatedNotFavoured: the nowhere horn yields no favouring of one candidate over another). Take the candidate z of the pair that is not a present input. By excluded middle its stand-in is contained in b, or not contained and produced by b, or neither (independent). The own-favouring bridge excludes the independent realm and the source-of-differences bridge excludes the merely produced item, so the stand-in is contained. The containment-recognition bridge then makes that stand-in a content about z that b itself apprehends, which is the cognition criterion's conclusion for b. The main theorem uses no axioms. The Comparator companion axiarchicControls (propext and Quot.sound, within the permitted Mathlib axiom set; Lane 4's carrier with the Lane 2b profiles and a new item type) gives the personal row with every premise and the criterion, and for each of the five non-logical premises a row where it alone fails and the criterion fails: contained but unapprehended stand-ins (recognition fails; the same stand-ins, relation and loci as the personal row), an independent realm (own-favouring fails), a produced realm (source-of-differences fails), one undifferentiated item with the good-tracking favouring (no item relation realizes it), and one item with a non-contrastive favouring that is good-general in the formal sense but favours an outcome over itself (irreflexivity fails). These are structural surrogates, not metaphysical possibilities; which account a row represents is an interpretive assignment.
